violation_type.title: Additional Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children Adjusting Appropriately for Different Ages and Abilities (26 TAC §747.1501(c)(4))
violation_type.short_title: Additional Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children Adjusting Appropriately for Different Ages and Abilities
violation_type.typical_finding: Recite: During the course of the investigation, it was determined that the permit holder is not properly supervising children in care due to her practice of going outside to smoke cigarettes while children are left alone indoors at least two times daily.    A keypad lock has been installed on the front door to help secure the home.

finding_variants.text: Recite: During the course of the investigation, it was determined that the permit holder is not properly supervising children in care due to her practice of going outside to smoke cigarettes while children are left alone indoors at least two times daily.    A keypad lock has been installed on the front door to help secure the home.
The caregiver was observed standing outside in the drivway talking with a visitor upon my arrival. There were 7 children ages 11 months to 8 years old in the home unsupervised.
During the investigation it was found that children are allowed to walk off the premises without supervision and down the street to another property and return to care.
3 children were observed to be asleep in a room that had 2 doors shut between them and the caregiver.     ** Caregiver opened both doors to regain auditory awareness of the children as they slept.8*
Three toddlers were laying awake in play pens in three seperate rooms with the door closed.
It was determined an infant was not properly supervised while in care, resulting in the child obtaining an injury to their arm.
